correctness.rationale: For N=2^k, k>=2, translation t→t+N/2 splits the N-point function space into equal +/- sectors labeled by first-coordinate parity. For first difference even and second odd, exact quadratic Gauss-sum squared modulus 2N is nonzero; all orthogonal frequencies within a sector therefore have the same second-coordinate parity. After removing the fixed chirp, dividing both coordinates by 2 reduces orthogonality to the level-(k-1) parabola. This gives a unique decomposition into two smaller bases and two parity bits, B_k=4 B_(k-1)^2, B_1=4 and B_k=2^(2^(k+1)-2). Inspected check_spectra.py provides finite checks only; the induction proves all k.
